examples.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Tangent or Cotangent
examples.problem: What is the general solution to the equation $\cot{x}=1?$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that $\cot{x}=\dfrac{1}{\tan{x}}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x_1 = \arctan \left( 1 \right)= \dfrac{\pi}{4}
$$

The tangent function has a period of $\pi.$  Therefore, the general solution for the given equation is: 

$$
x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is any integer.

feedback.problem: What is the general solution to the equation $5\operatorname{csc}⁡x+10=0?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{csc}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{csc}⁡x+10 & =0 \\ 5\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-10 \\ \operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{csc}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\text{arcsin}(-\frac{1}{2})=-\frac{\pi }{6}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $4$th quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{6}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/85b7b73fa793153cfedb2ffdb6825edd0845f93dbb472404862a78476a56fc35.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the given equation is

$$
x=-\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{7\pi }{6}+2n\pi .
$$

Writing this as $x=\theta +2n\pi ,$ where $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ we get

$$
x=\frac{7\pi }{6}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{11\pi }{6}+2n\pi .
$$
